sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Preble County
sections.html:
The Preble County Recorder is on the second floor of the courthouse, 101 E. Main Street, Eaton, OH 45320, phone (937) 456-8173. Weekday service runs until 4:30 in the afternoon, yet the courthouse front door is locked at 4:00, so get there early. Check with the office about holiday hours before you plan a trip around a closing date.

The county has 40,999 residents, 16,412 households and 18,093 housing units, 9.3% of them vacant. Owners live in 76.7% of occupied homes, so most deeds pass between owner-occupants. Expect questions about the grantee's tax mailing address and marital status at the counter.

The printed schedule is short. One flat price covers a deed, mortgage, affidavit, easement, land contract, lease, mechanic's lien, trust or power of attorney: $39.00 through page two, then $8.00 for every added page. A marginal notation is $4.00.

  • Certified copies are $2.00 per page, with $1.00 more for each seal.
  • A document that misses Ohio's standardization rules in R.C. 317.114 costs $20.00 more.
  • Court, tax authority, state and federal documents, plats and DD 214 discharges are exempt from that $20.00, as are papers signed before July 1, 2009.
  • Filing a military discharge, or getting a photocopy of one, is free.

The state fee statute, R.C. 317.32, makes up the two-page figure from two $17 shares plus an optional preservation charge of up to $5, which is how a county arrives at $39. Enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want the recorded paper returned by mail.

Following the county's formatting rules avoids the surcharge. Use white paper, letter or legal size, with black or blue ink and type of 10 point or larger. Submit an original rather than a copy, and skip highlighting and white-out.

  • Keep three inches clear at the top of page one for the recorder, auditor and engineer stamps.
  • Keep an inch and a half clear at the top of later pages, and an inch at the sides and bottom.
  • Show who prepared the document, and type or print a name below any signature that is hard to read.
  • State the grantor's marital status, and give the grantee's tax mailing address.
  • Include a full legal description and prior recording information, approved by the engineer before recording.

The grantor signs and acknowledges the deed before a notary public. The conveyance document must also carry the stamps of the county engineer and county auditor showing the grantor complied with R.C. 319.202.

The auditor's conveyance fee is three dollars for each $1,000 of price, with a 50 cent transfer fee per parcel. The auditor's counter is on the second floor of the same courthouse, (937) 456-8148, and the deed is stamped there before it goes to the recorder.

A county commission may also adopt a transfer tax of up to 30 cents per $100, which R.C. 322.02 assigns to the grantor and routes through the auditor. Before you total your net proceeds, ask whether Preble County has one in place.

The Office of Land Use Management, at 937-456-8171 on the first floor, answers questions about property splits and building permits. A lot split matters if you are selling only part of a parcel, since the engineer must approve the legal description.

sections.h2: Courthouse offices for a home sale
sections.html:
All three main offices share the courthouse, so a seller can finish most of the errands in one trip.

Preble County courthouse offices for a home sale
OfficeUsed forPhone
RecorderRecording deeds, mortgages and releases(937) 456-8173
AuditorConveyance fee, transfer, valuation complaints(937) 456-8148
TreasurerPaying property tax(937) 456-8140

Tax payments are taken on the second floor at the treasurer's office. The sheriff's office handles sheriff's sales on Fridays at 9 a.m. in the first-floor lobby of the courthouse, which is where a foreclosure sale of a Preble County home would be held.

sections.h2: Order of steps for a Preble County deed
sections.html:
The usual path runs through three desks in the courthouse.

  1. Prepare the deed with the formatting rules above, including the marital status of the grantor and the grantee's tax mailing address.
  2. Sign and acknowledge it before a notary public.
  3. Have the engineer approve the legal description if it is new or only part of a parcel is changing hands.
  4. Take it to the auditor for the stamp and the conveyance fee.
  5. Take it to the recorder, pay the recording fee, and include a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want it mailed back.

The recorder offers an online search index, a title fraud service and a fraud sleuth profile through its page. Online indexes start December 14, 1999, through a CountyFusion site, and the Ohio Recorders Association page for Preble County links to the same system. For older deeds, you need to visit the office or ask staff.

The recorder keeps a complete, accurate and permanent record of documents that convey or burden land, used by attorneys, historians, genealogists and land title examiners. If you are tracing an old farm or a family transfer, ask for the volume and page once you find the entry in the index.

Owners who are worried about forged deeds can register for the free title fraud service.

sections.h2: Board of Revision and your value
sections.html:
The Board can lower or raise a value, but only on a complaint filed inside the window. The auditor takes DTE Form 1 in the first quarter after the tax year, with a cutoff of 4:30 in the afternoon on March 31 at the auditor's office. Mail counts if it is postmarked by that day.

Three people sit on the Board: the auditor, the treasurer and a commissioner or the commissioner's representative. Its authority comes from R.C. 5715.13 through 5715.19. Questions go to (937) 456-8197 or (937) 456-8131. A late or defective complaint may be dismissed without a hearing, so file early.

A sale sometimes pulls in other offices. Evictions and small claims are heard by the Eaton Municipal Court at 1199 Preble Drive, phone 937-456-4941. Probate Court, second floor, 937-456-8137, handles name changes and marriage licenses. The Clerk of Courts has the third floor, 937-456-8160.

Sheriff's sales run on Fridays beginning at 9 a.m. in the first-floor lobby, and the sheriff's office at 937-456-6262 has details. A seller facing one of those sales or a tenant dispute can still deal with the recorder and auditor in the usual order, but should line up the court side first.

If paperwork, a tenant or a pending sale is slowing you down, a cash buyer such as Cash Home Buyers CA can close without a lender's appraisal, though the deed still goes through the auditor and recorder.

faqs.q: How much does the Preble County recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: $39.00 covers the first two pages and each added page is $8.00. A marginal notation is another $4.00, and a nonconforming paper adds $20.00.
Three dollars per $1,000 of price plus fifty cents a parcel, paid to the auditor ahead of recording.

faqs.q: What time does the recorder's office close?
faqs.a: Service runs to 4:30 on weekdays, but the courthouse front door locks at 4:00. Get there before 4:00, or call (937) 456-8173 if you are running late.

faqs.q: Can I get my DD 214 from the recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. Military discharge papers are kept at the recorder's office, and filing a discharge or getting a photocopy of it carries no fee.

faqs.q: When does the Board of Revision take complaints?
faqs.a: From January 1 to March 31 of the year after the tax year, with a cutoff of 4:30 in the afternoon on March 31 at the auditor's office. Mailed ones need a postmark by then.
